issues.legal_issue: A tenant is not shown to be habitually in arrears where the landlord repeatedly accepts belated rent without objection or warning and does not demand regular payment before seeking eviction on that ground.
material_facts: The tenant paid rent in lump sums covering several months, with payments made at intervals rather than monthly.
The landlord repeatedly accepted the belated payments without objection.
The landlord did not warn the tenant to pay regularly or otherwise indicate that the delayed payments were unacceptable.
The Rent Controller and appellate authority found against eviction on the arrears ground, but the High Court reversed that finding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not right to reverse the concurrent finding that the tenant was not liable to eviction as a habitual defaulter; the appellate authority’s order was restored and the tenant’s appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 13(3)(ii) of the C.P. and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949 requires the tenant to be habitually in arrears; unlike provisions that make non-payment for a specified period sufficient, mere delayed payment does not itself establish that condition. Under S.P. Deshmukh v. Shah Nihal Chand Waghajibai Gujarati, [1977] 3 SCC 515, a contrary agreement may be inferred from the parties’ conduct over time, and payments need not follow a fixed interval. The landlord’s conduct in accepting delayed rent is crucial: acceptance under protest accompanied by a warning does not imply agreement to altered payment terms, whereas repeated unprotested acceptance without notice prevents the landlord from suddenly seeking eviction; the landlord should demand regular payment if intending to insist on it. Pandurang Tukaram Rajkondawar v. Salaram Madhaorao Chavan, [1985] Mh. L.J. 169; Shishir Hari Mahajan v. Sanarasiobai Rodmal Sharma, [1982] Mh. L.J. 908; and Nathuji Narayanrao Udapure v. Narendra Vasanjibhai Thakkar, [1981] Mh. L.J. 446 were referred to, but the Court rejected the contention that an implied arrangement could be inferred only where payments followed a fixed interval.

rule.if: habitual_arrears_eviction_case and repeated_late_rent_payments and landlord_accepted_late_rent_without_objection and not landlord_warned_or_demanded_regular_payment

predicates.habitual_arrears_eviction_case: The proceeding sought eviction on the ground that the tenant was habitually in arrears with rent.
predicates.repeated_late_rent_payments: The tenant repeatedly paid rent late, including in payments covering several months.
predicates.landlord_accepted_late_rent_without_obje: The landlord repeatedly accepted the late rent without objecting to the timing of payment.
predicates.landlord_warned_or_demanded_regular_paym: The landlord warned the tenant to pay regularly or demanded regular payment before seeking eviction.
predicates.tenant_not_established_as_habitual_defau: The tenant was not established as a habitual defaulter for the purpose of eviction.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding alleges habitual arrears, repeated late payments accepted without objection and without a warning or demand for regular payment mean that the tenant is not established as a habitual defaulter.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings that a landlord failed to prove bona fide requirement should not be disturbed where no acceptable ground for interference is shown.
material_facts: The Rent Controller and the appellate authority considered the relevant circumstances and found that the landlord had not proved bona fide requirement.
The High Court reconsidered the record and confirmed that finding.
No acceptable ground for interfering with the concurrent findings was shown in the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent findings on bona fide requirement were left undisturbed, and the landlord’s appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no acceptable ground to interfere with the concurrent factual findings of the Rent Controller, the appellate authority and the High Court on the landlord’s failure to prove bona fide requirement.

predicates.appeal_challenging_bona_fide_requirement: The appeal challenged a finding concerning whether the landlord had a bona fide requirement for eviction.
predicates.concurrent_finding_that_requirement_not_: The lower decision-makers consistently found that the landlord had not proved bona fide requirement after considering the relevant circumstances.
predicates.no_acceptable_ground_to_interfere: No acceptable basis for disturbing the concurrent findings was shown.
predicates.concurrent_finding_left_undisturbed: The concurrent finding that bona fide requirement was not proved remained in place.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a concurrent finding that bona fide requirement was not proved and shows no acceptable ground for interference, that finding remains undisturbed.
